gates.title: Install the workspace app on the Enterprise Grid org
gates.detail: Create a Slack app from slack/manifest.json and install it on the Enterprise Grid org, not on a single workspace. Grant it to workspaces created later, and approve it if an admin must. This app only creates workspaces. It is not the Salesforce for Slack app, and it does not post Salesforce updates. Skip this when that org install already exists.

gates.title: Store the org-admin Slack token
gates.detail: Keep the org-admin user token, the one with admin.teams:write, in the coding agent's secret store. The agent uses it only to create a workspace. Do not put it in a Salesforce named credential. Keep it out of git. Skip this when it is already stored.

gates.title: Connect the Salesforce org to seed
gates.detail: Sign the coding agent into the Salesforce org that should receive the records. A demo org is the usual choice. The agent uses whichever org that login opens. This login does not connect Slack.

gates.title: Connect this workspace with Salesforce for Slack
gates.detail: Do this for every new workspace. Add the Salesforce for Slack app to that workspace and connect it to the Salesforce org you seeded. In Salesforce, finish Initial Slack Setup if this org is not already allowed to connect. That native connector is how records show up in Slack. Do not replace it with a flow, a named credential, or a call to chat.postMessage.

gates.title: Deploy metadata only if the agent is refused
gates.detail: The agent creates custom objects and custom fields through the Salesforce connection, and deploys Apex with the Salesforce CLI. Do this in Setup only when that login cannot deploy. Otherwise leave it to the agent.
